<p>&nbsp;</p>
These exercises are about extending an AI assistant with instruction files and skills.

**Do not paste protected or unpublished data into any AI tool.**

**Exercise 1** - **Before and after CLAUDE.md**

- Make a new folder on your computer and open a new project in your agent software within that folder.
- Make another folder within that folder called 'key_data'
- Copy the small RNAseq results table in the *docs/data* folder of this course named *small_DEtable.csv* to this new 'key_data' folder you have created.  
- Ask your agent to modify this file in some way (e.g. 'read in the csv file in the 'key_data' folder and add a column called 'user' and fill it in with scientist@ru.edu')
- What happens?

- Now make a CLAUDE.md file and include an instruction that should prevent the agent from modifying that file. 
- Put that CLAUDE.md file into the same folder as your current session
- Ask the agent again to modify this file. 
- Is the behavior different?

- If you ask the agent explicitly to modify the original table and say it has permission to do so, what happens then?

```{asis, echo=toMessage}
What happened? Before having a CLAUDE.md file (see text from example file below) the agent freely added the column to the table. After including the CLAUDE.md file below, the same prompt led the agent to save a new version of the table with the new column without modifying the original table.

When explicitly asked to modify that table, and saying it was okay to do so, the agent added the column. Though in this case it did ask and confirm this is what I wanted to do.

Take home: CLAUDE.md file is a guide for the agent, but it can be over ruled over the course of the conversation if the agent believes it has permission to do so.


Example CLAUDE.md for second part of question:

# CLAUDE.md

## Things you can't do
- never modify any files that are in the 'data' folder

 
```

**Exercise 2** - **Write a skill from scratch**

- Using the RNAseq results table in the *docs/data* folder named *p53_null_minus_p53_WT_DGE.csv*, develop a skill that produces a useful report that could be re-used for any future RNAseq results. 

  - The report should at minimum contain the input table in an interactive format and a scatter/volcano plot showing log2FoldChange vs significance of change (e.g. absolute value of stat column or -log10(p)).  Include anything else you think could be helpful in documenting this experiment.   
  - The skill should save a .qmd or .Rmd file that produces the report and could be run in the future to reproduce the analysis (not a static html report that isn't generated by R or Python code)
  - If you have Claude Code or Codex, save the skill in a format and location where it can only be accessed within a specific project folder and not globally on your system. 
  - What kind of approach do you want to take? Write the skills folder and SKILL.md file from scratch? Use the LLM model with the built in skill creator for the LLM model you are using? 
  
- Test the skill to make sure it is invoked when you prompt the model to make a differential expression report. 
  - Play with different prompts to test how effective the model is at activating the skill.
  
- Hint: an example report is in the */data* folder named *p53_null_minus_p53_WT_DGE_volcano_report.html* with an accompanying quarto (.qmd) script that generates that report. Feel free to go beyond this and add further analyses and information to the report your skill creates. 


```{asis, echo=toMessage}
The skill folder that generated the example report is here: */data/de-volcano-report-skill*. 

This was made by going back and forth with the assistant to produce code and iteratively test the output html report to make sure it was looking as expected. Once the desired report was achieved, the assistant then was asked to make a skill based on the quarto file and the conversation that produced the file.
```

 

**Exercise 3** - **Build a skill from a previous analysis**

- Think of an analysis you commonly perform where you ideally have one or more scripts carrying out this task/workflow. Identify where it would be useful to have a skill for any part of the process to help repeat this analysis in a reproducible manner. Make a skill for that task based on your previously existing scripts.  

  - Be specific in the inputs it should use, what the skills it should save. 
  - Determine whether this analysis should be one skill or multiple smaller, separate skills.
